raw_comment:
1. This Graph displays how the USA's use of energy sources has changed from 2001 to 2023. From 2002 to 2014, Coal was the main source of energy but has experienced a major downfall in recent years, dropping to only 16% usage. On the other hand, natural gas experienced an increase in usage, becoming the main energy source from 2016 to 2023. Wind energy has gone from barely being used to being responsible for 10% of energy. Other energy sources experienced fewer major changes.

2. I wonder how this switch from coal to natural gas has affected the environment. Natural gas has fewer emissions than coal, so this change could be positive. Will nuclear energy experience a decline as we continue to substitute harmful energy sources with friendly ones? With controversy around the use of windmills, will wind energy become insignificant again?

3. Energy production affects my electricity and the environment. I rely on the energy produced by these sources to power my home, providing me with light, internet, and running water. They also affect the state of the environment around me, usually in negative ways.

raw_comment:
1. The graph shows major energy sources in the U.S. and how their usage has changed in 22 years. From 2001 to early 2015 Coal was a major energy source for the U.S. As shown in the graph about 51% of the energy we consumed between 2001 and 2015 was powered by coal. Suddenly there was a shift in 2016 where coal no longer was the main source of energy but rather Natural Gas.

2. I wonder if Natural Gas will decline in the future due to the various alternatives that are more suitable for the environment. If we compare U.S. states and how their main energy source has impacted the condition of the state either negatively or positively, it's possible to find a less harmful or non-harmful energy source for the environment. 

3. The graph reflects how the United States has developed throughout the years, as the US developed so did our scientific knowledge, and this affected our lives greatly. We are constantly reminded of the harm we do to the environment. I believe that if we find better renewable energy sources and begin using them efficiently it will make a great change.  

4. A reflection of the advancement to finding a better alternative for non-renewable sources of energy in the United States.

Impact: several sources of energy negatively impact the climate and environment. Developments in technology may lead to cleaner and cheaper energy sources being more abundant. Future generations may suffer or thrive due to our current energy choices.

Headline- U.S. Energy Source Shifts Throughout the Years
This graph shows the different ways the United States has made energy from 2001-2023. It gives us an idea of how much our different sources of energy that we have access to are really being produced to make electricity. What I first noticed was the decline of coal in 2015 and how natural gas skyrocketed. Coal went from being over half our energy sources to now being roughly 10%. Natural gas has completely taken over. I also noticed how little we use solar and wind energy sources. They have increased throughout the years, which is really shocking to see. I wonder why this is. We are living in a such a modern century that one would think our energy sources have become less harmful. Why aren't we using these options which are better for the environment? I also wonder why nuclear energy spiked in 2020 then declined again, and is now shooting up once again. What caused the spike in the first place?  This is very applicable to me and my community. I and everyone around me use electricity every day. Basically, everything around us needs electricity to function. So, it's important to know where our electricity comes from and how it impacts our environment.

raw_comment:
Thanks to all the students who responded.   Here are some of the catchy headlines that we received:  “Shifting Winds: The Current of Energy Production in America” by Ava of Academy of Saint Elizabeth in Morris Township, N.J.; "U.S. Most Used Energy Sources: Is Gas Rising to the Top?" by Olivia of Barnstable High School in Mass.; “Coal to Sit the Bench": Renewable Energy to Overtake the Energy Giant” by Gavin and "The United States Energetic Change Towards Clean Energy" by Layla, both from Gull Lake High School in Richland, Mich.; and “A New Age of Energy! Natural Gas Overtakes Coal's Throne.” by Andres of Perth Amboy High School in N.J.

Please return on Friday when we will reveal the free link to the article that included this graph, a summary of the article, additional questions, shout outs for some of the best headlines for the graph and Stat Nuggets -- definitions of words that relate to the graphs and where you can find them in the graphs.

The next graph will be released by Friday, September 13.  The topic – 2024 Paris Olympics. 

Signing off – Sharon Hessney from Boston, who lives in a state which uses a lot of natural gas and could produce a lot of wind energy out in the Atlantic Ocean, but has not, and Corey Andreasen currently living in Qatar, who doesn't miss the rains of The Netherlands (yet)!

raw_comment: This graph is both very colorful and unique, while showing the rise and fall of certain energy resources. We can see that in more recent years, coal is out while natural gas is in. Other resources such as wind and solar energy have become quite popular. Nuclear energy also had a comeback in more recent years. We wonder why certain energy sources dropped and what caused this drop. Especially how they relate to events that happened in certain years. In our community, the surge of solar and wind energy has been shown to be effective all around. Businesses can be seen to be running on solar energy, and wind turbines are popping up more and more. Our title, reliable energy resources: what ate and what didn't.

raw_comment:
We notice this graph resembles a hybrid of a subdivided bar graph and a pie chart. The spikes in the blobs signify different energy passing another in the respective year. The difference in color indicates an identifier in group (hypro electric = blue, coal = black etc). It definitely provides a different approach in displaying data, and messages while combining traditional ways of representing data.

We wonder what the light grey represents and perhaps what events or legislative works influenced the rise and fall of the different energy sources. We also wonder about the purple blob at 2023, and which percentages align with the respective energy sources. 

Something we felt connected to our communities was the natural gas rising in recent years. There has been a lot of coverage and more activism surrounding pollution and climate change, and seeing a visual representation of that rise provides context to activist's worries. The drop in coal also shows a shift to slighter cleaner energy sources, which aligns with our modern day perspectives on climate change and in our community as well. 

Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.

Alike popular artist Chappell Roan's debut album "The Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess", we were thinking the graph's title could be "The Rise and Fall of American Fuel Source" !

1) I noticed that among all of the other sources of energy, natural gas had the largest uptick in the years from 2001 to 2023. Additionally, the amount of coal was drastically decreased in the same years, which was probably the reason that natural gas became so popular. 
2) I wonder what kind of a graph this is and how those who created it chose to use it as a representation of the conversion between sources. I also wonder what places specifically caused the most change in smaller industries like wind. It would have to be a rural area due to the amount of land needed to house a windmill farm of sorts. Therefore it is plausible that surrounding states of Idaho could have played a major role.

For example, some of our old tractors cannot have a GPS system that helps to drive and navigate in tough fields, whilst newer ones can. So that affects how and where we use each piece of machinery.
 4) Energy sources switch over the last 2 decades in the United States, causing an incredible flip in daily life for citizens everywhere!

raw_comment: The Graph represents the power produced by various energy sources within the past two decades. While analyzing, I noticed substantial fluctuations contributed by coal, natural energy, and nuclear energy. There seems to be a slow increase in wind and solar power, but hydroelectric remains at a steady 6%, spiking slightly in 2018. On the other hand, petroleum continues to serve as “liquid gold” for the American economy, but it is scarcely used because of its environmental detriments. In the United States, coal has historically been a significant source of electricity generation. However, its share in the energy mix has decreased over the years, as coal combustion releases pollutants such as sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, and particulate matter, a recipe for respiratory cancer. I wonder what the safest option for electricity would be regarding financing and the health of the people and the planet. Why are we not utilizing solar power more sparingly? As the third-largest and wealthiest nation in the world, the next step to bettering the well-being of the American people is choosing to spread funding for more appropriate energy sources like wind, solar, and renewable. In my neighborhood, most homes feature solar panels. This is a testament to the potential of solar energy to power homes, businesses, and even entire communities and a compelling reason to consider its widespread adoption.  Headline: Shifting Winds: the Current of Energy Production in America.

raw_comment: This graph is an image showing the types of power used to make electricity between 2001 and 2023 while also showing how it changed throughout the years. I noticed that coal was mainly used between 2001 and 2015 and then natural gas was mainly used. Other sources were also used during these times, but much less, and coal along with natural gas were the most prominent. Lastly, I noticed how solar power was introduced in 2013 and was a very nominal source, but began to grow. I wonder why in 2015 the United States switched from coal to natural gas and why they did not invest in the other types of energy that could have been used. This relates to me and my community because it shows us how we are getting electricity utilized in everyday life and also that the methods of getting electricity affect our environment. Along with this, I see how solar energy has become more common in the areas around me. I would headline this graph as Dramatic changes in power sources.

raw_comment:
1) I notice that over the years, there has been a decrease in the use of coal as a primary energy source. This decline has collided with the rise of natural gas, which has now become the leading energy source in many places. This transition is very interesting because it reflects a broader shift in how we produce and consume energy. As we move away from coal, we're impacting air quality and emissions levels. Natural gas burns cleaner than coal, resulting in lower levels of pollutants and greenhouse gases released into the atmosphere. The change highlights a growing awareness and responsibility toward adopting less harmful energy sources. 

2) What are the primary factors driving the transition from coal to natural gas as an energy source? Additionally, how have technological advancements made natural gas extraction more efficient, and how does the growing emphasis on sustainability influence how the public feels regarding energy sources.

3) The energy we use, either fossil fuels or renewable, affects the air quality in our community. Burning fossil fuels releases harmful pollutants that can cause health problems. In contrast, renewable energy produces little to no emissions, leading to cleaner air. By choosing renewable sources, we can improve our health and protect the environment for the future.

4)  Fossil Fuels Fade as Renewables Rise: A New Era of Clean Energy Begins!

raw_comment:
1) The things I notice in this graph on how energy sources have changed since 2001 are: Natural gas has increased, taking the lead from coal commissions, which highly decreased after being at its peak in 2014. Hydroelectric power stayed the same; it didn’t increase or decrease by any percentage. Wind and solar power increased highly while petroleum just went down.

2) I wonder why all of these changes have occurred in the world. Why this specific graph design and colors? Does this specific design mean or represent something specific or important that we should be aware of? Why did they change from mostly using coal commissions to using natural gasses? Did natural gasses worsen or improve electricity? Finally, I wonder why coal commissions were at their peak only until 2014 and why hydroelectric power stayed the same.

3) These changes on electricity from 2001 to 2023 relate to me and my community because electricity has changed more because of higher prices and a switch to renewable energy like solar and wind. These changes have helped reduce the use of fossil fuels, but it can be sort of expensive. The power grid has gotten better, and the power comes back after or doesn't leave while or after storms. Energy bills have gone up, but there are more options for clean energy. This has made a complicated but better environment for me and my community.

4) Colorful Explanation of Electricity Evolution (2001-2023)

raw_comment:
1) After a close observation of the graph, I've concluded that the use of coal as an energy source in the United States has significantly declined over the past two decades. This downtrend suggests a shift towards alternative energy sources, possibly driven by advancements in technology and concerns on global warming. The graph justifies my claim after revealing the use of coal as an energy source in the United States dropping down from 51% in 2002 to 18% in 2022. This is a whopping 33% decrease.

2) I wonder what's leading to this downtrend in coal usage. The statistical factors driving this change can range from data on energy consumption patterns or environmental factors. For example, a line graph analyzing the cost of coal over the last 2 decades, would reveal the financial correlation to the decline of coal usage for energy in the United States.

3)This relates to me and my community because coal once played a vital role in our town’s economy, as the Perth Amboy trains relied heavily on coal. The decline in coal usage reflects  technological advancements in the resources used to produce energy.  It’s important to consider how these changes may have affected a place like ours, where coal was once a valuable resource. This connection leads me to imagine how energy transitions impact  economies and even indexes (Dow Jones U.S. Coal Total Stock Market Index) as a market watcher myself.

4. Can we be approaching our first extinct energy source in the next couple of years?

Petroleum has the lowest percentage in the graph and hydroelectric energy retains the same percentage throughout the entire graph.

- To what extent will this affect our environment?

The change in coal and natural gas has environmental implications which could impact the quality of life in local communities, including cities like Perth Amboy. 

4) Headline
Natural Gas: The Fight for Cleaner Electricity Production

3)  The way these powers relate to me and my community through the use of it and making it able to function in our everyday life.

4) Power Produced in the U.S. Over Time

raw_comment:
It is noticeable that as coal decreases, natural gas increases. The decrease of the coal used for the production of energy dramatically decreased after 2014, which then led to natural gas to have an exponential increase at the same time. This shows that there's some sort of correlation between the two, since as one decreases one increases. Since there's a decrease-to-increase correlation, it raises multiple reasonable questions. Firstly, what is the reason for this dramatic change? (perhaps it is more efficient to use in the environment) Why is it that as nuclear energy increases, coal energy decreases even more? Is the main objective of using one energy source as opposed to another due to the efficiency of the energy in itself or merely for the sake of the environment?

This applies to not only my community, but as well as the U.S. nationally. It applies to my community insofar as the energy enables my society to function, without it we would pretty much go back to the stone ages. People need heating, transportation, electricity, etc in order to maintain their livelihood.

raw_comment:
1) I noticed that natural gas increased after 2016, and Wind did the same after 2018. Solar rapidly increased after 2014. Hydroelectric stays the same the entire time. Nuclear decreased then increased again, and Coal began as the largest and ended with Natural Gas being the largest.

2) I wonder why coal decreased as much as it did?  It seemed to happen rapidly as well, there was no buildup and now Natural Gas has the largest amount. Did everyone collectively decide to not use coal at all? I also wonder why hydroelectric stays the same the entire time? Each one has some sort of difference but hydroelectricity never changed.

3) This graph relates to my community and me when it comes to things like energy bills and the economy. Since this is showing me which energies are used the most, it can apply to how much energy we all use and why we may have to pay that much to begin with. The economy has recently been horrible as well and this graph goes all the way back to 2001, when it wasn't as bad as it was now.

4) The Energy Race

raw_comment:
What do you notice?: No two resources had drastic drops at the same time, neither did they have grand rises together. If you look at the graph bars you cannot see two rising enormously at the same exact time. Neither would you see two bars having extremely low drops in the same year. When a resource dropped, one always rose. Coal dropped drastically as seen in the graph, and natural gas began to rise. Nuclear dropped, and natural gas began to rise. Hydroelectric dropped, and wind began rise. A pattern is clearly shown here. 
What do you wonder?: I wonder why there was a constant pattern of when a resource dropped, another rose and took its place. Why did some resources go down some years, and up in other years? Why do we still use certain resources even if they're very harmful to our environment?
How does this relate to you and your community?: More and more homes in my community are beginning to use solar energy for power. Meaning other people residing in my town contribute to this graph because they're using solar energy for their electricity. This graph also shows how much the kinds of resources being used affect us because natural gas is now a highly used fuel, which is harmful to the environment because it involves the release of greenhouse gases in its production. Meaning, it is a danger to our health, and advances climate change. 
HEADLINE: Are We Killing Our Home, Our Earth?

raw_comment:
What do I Notice:
The graph shows the increase or decrease in energy resources across 22 years (2001-2023). Coal was the leading source until 2016 (51% dropping to 18%) when natural gas took over (17% rising to 42%). We also have other energy sources like Hydroelectric which stayed at 6% for the whole 22 years and Solar showing up in 2013 rising to 6%, even wind slowly increasing over the 22 years from less than 1% to now being 10%.
What do you wonder?
How did these changes come to be, was it some scientific discovery or was it found just to be easier to use these other resources?
How will these things change 22 more years into the future? My prediction is that solar and wind power will increase significantly.
How does this affect my community?
Everyone daily relies on some source of energy, in some communities these things don't matter but where I live I see it everywhere, and there are huge gas tanks. My town is where all the “ugliness” goes, so every day I'm affected slowly, i believe soon the energy resources will change to a much cleaner and better-looking source of energy.

raw_comment:
The graph contains information on the United State's various energy sources from 2001 to 2023. I noticed that the size of the blocks correlates with the amount of power that is produced from the following sources during that year. Up until 2015, coal was the major energy supplier to the United States followed by nuclear energy. While the use of coal as a source continues to decline, natural gas continues to rise, now making up 42% of the graph in 2023. I also notice that the use of wind as a source of energy starts to rise in 2007, while hydroelectric energy remains the same, solar energy starts to rise, and Petroleum decreases to almost undetectable. 
I wonder, however, why coal has had such a major decline during the same time period as natural gases uprising. I also wonder if this is due to the idea of natural gas being better for the environment than coal and if that idea is truly correct. Not only this, but I wonder why the rate of solar energy remains so low even though it has been heavily applied nation wide.
This relates to me and my community as, in my town, solar energy has been heavily implemented. Business buildings as well as houses have added solar panels as a healthier alternative to collect energy. Furthermore, everyday we rely on energy to give our homes and electric vehicles power in order to live comfortably. 
Catchy Headline: Electric Touch (America's Version) - The Energy Sources that Fuel the United States

raw_comment:
Headline: Dramatic Energy shifts are seen from 2001 to 2023
I notice that the use of coal to make electricity has significantly decreased. However, the use of natural gas to create electricity has increased. Solar and wind electricity have slightly increased. Nuclear power had some ups and downs but as of now is at almost the same as it was in 2001. Petroleum was slightly used for electricity in 2001 but now is not at all in 2023. Hydroelectric power increased and decreased, therefore staying the same.  I wonder what led to the significant decrease in coal electricity. I also wonder if natural electricity “replaced” coal electricity in a way since the increase of natural gas is similar in size to the decrease of coal.  I think that this graph is comparing the different types of electricity.  By comparing the percentages, people can make claims regarding different types of electricity. This relates to me and my community because every day we use energy. Knowing there has been a shift to better electricity sources could mean cleaner air and better health.

raw_comment:
In the graph, I noticed that natural gas surpassed coal as the leading energy source around 2016.  I noticed that nuclear power had been the second most produced energy source in 2001, while it then dropped down to third just to rise back to second around 2022/2023.  The decline of coal must have impacted many companies as well as the increase of natural gas.  I wonder if the world realized the harmful side effects of coal around this time, resulting in the decrease of coal emissions and the rise of the use of natural gas.  I also wonder if nuclear power declined just to increase again; possibly because it is a cleaner energy source.  I also wonder if the hydroelectric, wind, solar, and petroleum energy sources are expensive or not as effective since they are at the bottom 22%.  This relates to my community because many people in my town have recently gotten solar panels on their roofs, which I have noticed in the last year.  This not only helps the environment but is also a turn towards the direction of cleaner energy overall.

raw_comment:
From 2001 to 2023, the graph shows a significant shift in U.S. electricity generation sources. Coal use has declined sharply, while natural gas has seen substantial increases. Other renewable resources such as wind and solar have started to increase their role. Nuclear and hydroelectric power have remained relatively stable, with petroleum's role in electricity generation remaining minimal. This transition reflects broader trends toward cleaner energy and reduced reliance on fossil fuels. What I wonder is why petroleum no longer has any use and why it never truly had a massive purpose. As for my community, the shift towards renewable energy sources like wind and solar, and away from coal, could mean cleaner air and potentially lower energy costs for my community.

raw_comment: Something that I noticed in the graph is the dramatic decrease in coal as an energy source, as well as the dramatic increase in natural gas' use. I also noticed how more environmentally friendly energy sources are still at the bottom, despite steadily increases over the years. I wonder if the dramatic changes between natural gas and coal has something to do with resource scarcity, as well as the change to a more robotic workforce. As somebody who does not live in a rural area, it is important to not only me, but my community to understand the changes in energy sources so that we may advocate for more renewable energy sources, as well as to be more mindful with our electricity usage for the sake of our environment. The headline I chose for the graph is "The Rise of Natural Gas as an American Energy Source" because it can address the major change in natural gas as an energy source in America, which goes unbeknownst to many.

raw_comment:
1. What I noticed
I noticed that that most of U.S. energy production was reliant on coal before taking a sharp fall to natural gases around 2015, and after, proceeds to battle with nuclear energy for more production, exchanging leads after 2019.
2. What I wonder
I wonder why the dominance of coal in U.S. energy production fell so sharply and seems to be falling even more as time passes. Is it legislation, and if so, why were there so many changes during the Trump administration?
3. The different uses of fuel in the country can directly affect me and my community, by the changing of prices and amounts. Different fuel uses by our government can lead to prices ranging differently, which can directly affect the average American.
4. "America's Decisions Regarding Fuels"

raw_comment:
I noticed that from 2001-2016 coal was the predominant energy source for the US, with nuclear and natural gas being the closest competitors. I wonder what influenced the decline of nuclear energy.  It's one of the more sustainable and cleaner forms of energy, yet one of the underutilized forms. It's interesting the popularity natural gas has garnered in the United States.  I can see this in my community because the energy price has only been on the rise and when I look at my parents' bills out of sheer boredom. I've noticed the significance that natural gas plays in our energy consumption.  
" Energy in a blink"

raw_comment:
2002-2014 America's biggest use for electricity was coal, which then got replaced by natural gas. Coal is still used quite a bit along with nuclear product. Hydroelectric, wind, solar, and petroleum are also used to create electricity across the country. 
What will this graph turn out to be in the coming years? How much different will it be in 2045 v.s. now? Will something else become the biggest source of will it stay as natural gas?

The Problems of the Amount of Products Used to Make Electricity

raw_comment:
What stands out to me the most in this graph is that coal and natural gas have been the two main powerhouses regarding how the US makes electricity. Regarding this, I also noticed how coal declined for the first time in 2015/2016 natural gas shot up and stayed up while coal kept rising and declining. I wonder why we as a country do not try and use hydroelectric, solar, and wind energy more often. They are not only less harmful to the environment but they are also renewable resources meaning they never run out. Does it have to do with money, accessibility, or the fact that some things can't be powered by water, wind, and sun? This is extremely applicable to my life and community because I use electricity every single day and honestly could not live without it. At my school, we use electricity for the ovens in the kitchen, the fridges in the kitchen, the smart boards in most classes, and the ac in some classes.

Electricity affects every community everyday. Almost everyone in the world uses energy, I am right now typing this. Humans are blissfully unaware of how much energy we use on a day to day basis. raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I noticed that until around 2015, the largest percentage of power was produced from coal. After that, natural gas and other methods of power production became used more often, and coal was used to produce power less often. I also noticed that in 2020, there was a noticeable increase in power produced from nuclear energy and a noticeable decrease in coal. However, around 2021, the percentage of nuclear energy and coal used for power production rose/dropped to around the percentage that they were before 2020. Another observation I had was that the use of petroleum for power production has become almost minuscule compared to other power sources as the years progressed.

What do you wonder?
I wonder if we will see the same trend of coal being used less for power production in the upcoming years. I also wonder if petroleum being used as an energy source will completely disappear from the graph in the future because it is already being used so little now in comparison to other energy sources.

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me and my community because we all need power in our daily lives to perform functions. Fossil fuels are an energy source to power all of our technology from the washing machine to the lights. The community and I use electricity and power every day. 

Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
"Energy Sources and Fossil Forces; How Power Production Evolved"

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
The biggest thing I noticed was the drastic change in American energy sources. From 2001 to 2015 coal was the US's number one energy source at 51% . Since 2015 natural gas has outgrown coal as the US's main energy source. Natural gas has risen from 17% to 42%. And coal has taken a backseat lowering down to 18%.

What do you wonder?
I wonder what happened during 2014-2015 to change the look of US energy sources so drastically. Could it relate to climate change concerns? I also wonder how this has changed the US's power grid, since many power plants who burn coal to supply power, and having to change with the ever changing energy market how much time did it take for them to transfer over to produce other forms of energy?

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to my community because a lot of the farmland around the area have be purchased and or have gotten offers to sell in order to build solar panels on the races of farmland. This is both concerning and easing to me because it shows that the US is making an effort to change its past ways of burning coal and hurting the environment but its also concerning because it may be harming the environment in a different way. How will these solar farms affect the wildlife of the area?

Catchy Headline
"Coal taking a backseat as natural gas rises to the top"

raw_comment:
I notice that natural gas and coal switched positions for main sources of energy throughout the 20 years. We also see a rise in wind and solar energy that offers a much cleaner basis of energy. Nuclear energy is on the rise as well. Overall nuclear energy is extremely clean unless there is a natural disaster. Even though we are pushing for safer and cleaner energy, natural gas still seems to be a necessity for our power grids.

I wonder when natural gas will be overtaken by a new energy source. I could see solar energy being the newer power source along with nuclear energy. With time going forth there will be new ways for power without relying on dirty sources.

In my community, our power seems to be fueled by natural gas. As we go further away, there seems to be a huge growth in solar energy. With fields full of solar panels that move with the sun's rays. I believe that solar energy is the most efficient way to power if everyone jumps on board to it.

The Fall of Natural Resources? Time for Renewable Energy to Power a new Future.

raw_comment:
I noticed that coal became less prevalent after 2016 when natural gas came into the spotlight. Solar wasn’t even in the picture until after 2014. Nuclear power has stayed relatively the same in terms of popularity, with a few waves across the years. Wind and hydroelectric also have similar stakes in energy percentages. 

I wonder what outliers or biases exist in this data. Are there any categories that we missed? Are there any forms of energy that are coming out now that could turn this graph upside down and change the concept of renewable energy as we know it?

Clean energy has a hold on everyone whether they like it or not. We live in Michigan (aka the Great Lakes State), so it’s interesting to see what amazing things water can do in terms of generating energy. Water in of itself is a powerful force, so it’s not a big surprise that we found a way to harness that and apply it to more mechanical outlets.

Headline: Gas is the Backbone of America...Who Knew?

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that we have had an increasing reliance on natural gas now in 2023 with 42% of our energy coming from this source compared to the 17% in 2001. I also realize we have used significantly less coal over time as it has fallen from 51% to approximately 16%. I notice that the “sustainable” forms of energy production have not had significant change over the past despite the billions of dollars we have put into sustainable energy programs in the past.

What do you wonder?
I wonder why coal became so much less prominent around the year 2016 and why natural gas came to replace its spot as what we rely on the most for our energy production. I also wonder what we can do to decrease our reliance on natural gas, which is a finite resource, without spending trillions.

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to my community because if the government is putting billions and increasing our sustainable energy infrastructure, we will start to see more and more solar panels and wind farms. I noticed last year on a drive to Purdue University the hundreds of wind turbines scattered across the fields. At the MSU campus, I noticed parking shelters that had solar panels fitted on the top to generate energy. I think we will see a lot of this over the past couple of years.

Title: One pollutant was replaced with another. Why did this happen and what can we do to have more sustainable energy practices?

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
Within this graph, I notice that from the earlier years like 2002, every way of electricity was a lot more spread out. It was more equally spread out. Coal had the biggest impact in 2002,exactly 51% of electricity came from it and now natural gas has the biggest impact in 2024, with 42% of electricity formed from it. I also noticed that the amount of wind electricity increased so it's actually a way now unlike 2002. 

What do you wonder?
Something that I wonder is why are our safe ways of getting electricity not higher throughout these 22 years. You have solar power, which I understand is expensive but it saves so much money in the long term and it's only at 6%. Hydroelectric is another, it has remained at 6% since 2002-2024.
 
How does this relate to your community?
This relates to my community because most people want to use the cheaper options, which are the most toxic and harmful to our environment. There needs to be a way to make the safer options less expensive.

Catchy Headline:
"Charge Up in the US"

raw_comment:
I noticed that from 2001 to 2014, the United States relied on coal for its electricity . After 2014, the use of coal for electricity began to take a steep fall, while the use of natural gas for electricity rose. Natural gas usage in the United States has risen from about 17% in 2001 to 42% in 2023. Nuclear and hydroelectric electricity usage remain approximately the same in 2023 as it did in 2001, but solar electricity usage seems to be on the rise, starting around 2012. 

While studying the graph, I immediately noticed the large dip in coal usage for electricity from 2014 to 2016. I wonder what caused this dip. Was this dip due to an increase in awareness of global warming? Upon taking a deeper look into the graph, I observed that when petroleum usage declined, solar usage became popular. I ponder what caused the switch from petroleum usage to solar usage.

In my community, people are realizing the effect that excessive usage of harsh forms of electricity has on our community. Our community as a whole recognizes that we need to try and cut back on our electricity usage, or at least use electricity in a more efficient and environmentally friendly manner. Some ways my community has taken the initiative include adding new solar panels and creating more windmills. When driving into other towns, I have noticed less solar panels and windmills than in my community which suggest that my community is trying to actively lessen climate change. 

Coal is Only for Christmas

raw_comment:
What do you notice? 
I notice that coal dominated the electricity production until around 2015 when it began to have a downfall. At that same time, natural gas took it's spot as the most used source of electricity. Petroleum is the least used substance and has stayed at the bottom throughout the years. At natural gas’s first transcend in 2005, nuclear source fell. As one source gains more usage, another loses it. 

What do you wonder?
I wonder why coal lost it's dominance so aprubtly. What was the trigger that caused natural gas to take it's place? What benefits do certain sources bring? I wonder if nuclear’s spike in 2020 was in relation to Covid- 19. I also wonder why petroleum is so rarely used.

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me and my community because it ties in with the economy. Every source  
has a different price that comes with it, and majority will want to use the cheapest 
source. This is the reason as to why some sources are more used than others. The 
abundance of a certain source also affects which ones will become more popular. 
 
Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
“Natural gas has all the class”

raw_comment:
What do you notice? 
I noticed that from 2001-2015 the use of coal for electricity was superior to all others. Closer to 2001 it was over 50 percent of the electricity but moving on it still remained number one just steadily decreasing a little. During this time natural gas was on the rise rather than declining. I also noticed that hydraulic and nuclear remained pretty steady not changing over time.

What do you wonder?
I really wonder why coal disappeared how it did. It went from being the top source for years and years to the next year being down almost 30%. I am also curious why not use more hydraulic and wind powered electricity? It is healthy for the earth unlike the most common sources still. I wonder if these changes are because they realize whats safer for the earth or lack of material? 

How does this relate to you and your community? 
Burning these fossil feels really impacts the entire world including me and my community causing global warming for all. If there isn't a change this will continue for a lot longer and cause even more issues and global warming in the world. Also in my community I am seeing an uprise on solar paneled electricity which is definitely a good thing and I will hopefully see this trend continue.

raw_comment:
I noticed that in just six years, there was a large shift in how the United States made electricity. From 2014-2020, three major changes occurred. First, the made amount of natural gas overtook that of coal, which had previously dominated electricity production 15 years prior. Next, around 2019, wind energy became more used than hydroelectric. Although small percentages, the change could be considered major considering how long hydroelectric energy designs have been put to use. Lastly, around 2020, nuclear energy majorly spiked, taking over coal, which had begun considerably decreasing five years leading up to this switch.

I wonder why although the graph represents percentages of energy creation relating to the thickness of the lines, what the crossing of the lines represent exactly. I also wonder what exactly lead to these switches in the energy creation.

The information in this graph relates to my community because it provides a statistic that helps a smaller community, like the town I live in, to better understand the energy they use everyday, and how that may compare to the rest of the United States.

"The United States Energetic Change towards Clean Energy"

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
For this graph, I notice that from 2002-2016, Coal had a vast impact on the ways Americans produced electricity. It took up approximately 51% of the total methods used to create energy. 
What do you wonder?
I wonder why Solar Power hasn’t advanced to more than 6% considering it has little to no disadvantages and issues. Solar power and hydroelectric are possibly less effective but better for the environment. Solar energy can be very strong and useful and I am curious why these methods haven’t been urged to explore more. 
How does this relate to your community?
Energy is what communities and towns/cities need to have in order to run properly. 
Energy permeates through many different aspects and functions in our lives. We need to make sure that the energy we are using is affordable for everyone in the community, and energy that is efficient and healthy to put out onto our earth. 

Headline: 

“The Evolvement of Multifariousness Energies”

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I noticed that there were only 5 electricity sources in 2002, this number increased to 7 electricity sources by 2014 as solar and wind were introduced as an energy source. The 2 combined make up 16% of electricity in America in 2014 whereas it was seemingly 0% in 2002.

What do you wonder?
I wonder where solar and wind will sit on this graph in another 12 years. I wonder this as it seems that solar and wind as an electricity source is on the rise. With new policies, ideas, and strong opinions about clean energy, I can make the assumption that both solar and wind will take up a much larger portion of the graph than before. 

How does this relate to you and your community?
If the same assumptions are made as me within the community, we can reasonably start/increase investing in wind turbines and solar farms to power our school, town, and surrounding homes. 

Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
“Electricity in The United States by percentage, and the rise of new sources”

Was our access to coal restricted due to used-up resources or international affairs? I wonder why nuclear and coal was used almost equally from 2019 - 2023.

It changes what the future of the earth looks like for us and for generations to come. As more sustainable electricity sources increase we may see more windmills or it may become more common to own solar panels.

-I noticed that coal went from producing half of the U.S.’ energy to only generating about 18% today. I notice that Natural gas is now the leading source of energy for the U.S. providing 42% of the total energy. Nuclear and Hydroelectric sources provide nearly the same amount of energy today as they did in 2002. Solar is the only energy that did not even provide a single percent in 2002 that is on the graph today.
-I wonder why Nuclear and hydroelectric energy have not changed almost at all. I wonder how much of the percentage solar energy will take up in ten years. I wonder why natural gas is the leading energy source. I wonder why Petroleum is even on this graph.

We have not been building any new dams so it makes sense that hydroelectric energy is not changing. Wind turbines are popping up around the area which is contributing to the wind energy growth.
-“Coal to sit the bench": Renewable energy to overtake the energy giant.

raw_comment:
-I noticed that coal was a very popular strategy to create electricity in the United States until about 2015; after 2015 natural gas was easily the most popular way. I also noticed that hydroelectric, wind, solar, and petroleum all stayed as a minimal percentage of electricity actions across the nation.
-As I studied the graph, there were lots of changing aspects to the graphs which had me wondering about many perspectives. First of all, I wondered why the natural gas production started out so low around 2002 and increased to the most abundant way by 2016. Similarly, I noticed how the coal shrunk down to nearly half the percentage by 2016 as it had in 2002. This led me to wondering how the community decided that coal was not good or logical for making electricity; did they question the safety hazards or did they just find a more efficient way to produce electricity?
-This is related to my community because energy is a utility we use every day of our lives. Most people do not even recognize the amount of electricity we use daily (we use electricity for our dishwashers, showers, lights, etc.). Similarly, in my community I have seen the production of energy by using windmills out in the country with wind, which is an uncommon way to produce electricity, but is a very safety-conscious strategy.
Catchy Headline: Electricity Efficiency or Safety Standards?

raw_comment:
-I noticed that there are considerable changes around 2014 to 2016, as natural gas surpasses coal as an energy source. Solar energy, it can be surmised that this is from the rise of rooftop solar, is rising in use. Later, I noticed that around roughly 2020, wind power sources surpassed hydroelectric, and nuclear surpassed coal energy. 

-I wonder why these changes are occurring, as it could be policy, efficiency, or concern for the planet, or simply the accumulation of the aforesaid. As there has been much discussion over the past many years, I believe it is an effort to turn to more green methods, as mentioned above. 

-This affects myself and the community around me due to both the facilities we have, and the energy we consume. The different types of energy supply various facilities and are used by different properties and people for various reasons, many who do not know the origin of this amenity. 

-“Sources of Energy within the US: The Fall of Coal”

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that in the period of 2014-2015 the use of coal greatly decreased, while the use of natural gasses transcended.  In the period of 2004-2006, natural gasses had a drastic increase, while nuclear decreased. There seems to be an inverse trend that when one energy source increases, another one decreases. When looking at the wind, hydroelectric, and solar energy sources, their use hovered around the same throughout the years.

What do you wonder?
I wonder why there is an inverse relationship between sources that increase and decrease. What happened in these periods that caused the switch to happen? Why is coal such a big contributor in 2002-2014, but suddenly drops and allows natural gasses to surpass it. 

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to the community because certain energy sources allow for things to be created and used, which is vital to evolving technology. As new sources permeate through different cities as towns, it can strongly affect the future of that area and what they are capable of producing. This relates to me, because I personally use these things in my daily life, even if it goes unnoticed. For example, the electricity in my house and places I go to is generated by natural gas, coal, and nuclear energy.

HEADLINE
Out with the "coal" and in with the new

raw_comment:
I notice that energy based on coal filters out while natural gas goes up. Also as soon as coal dropped, natural gas shot way up in usage. I also noticed that wind and solar-powered energy have risen over the past few years.

I wonder why coal usage decayed so quickly in 2014-2016. I also wonder why nuclear energy keeps going up and down over the years.

This relates to the community by showing the growth of conservation. As seen at the bottom, solar energy and wind-powered energy are transcending each year. They haven’t dropped yet. This goes along with the dropping of coal used as fuel. When coal burns, it emits toxins that can cause acid rain and respiratory issues. Using things like wind and solar panels to gain energy that’s safe for humans and the environment seems like a win-win. It shows how the community is slowly adapting to the technology to healthily generate energy. However, natural gas is still in first place since it’s more convenient and cheaper.

1. Over the last decade, the use of coal as an energy source has decreased greatly, replaced by natural gas. Furthermore, clean energy sources like solar, wind, and hydroelectric power have been picking up popularity.

4. Coal is so last decade

raw_comment:
Over the years, the use of coal declined nearly 40%, whereas the use of natural gas increased by around 25%. Also in 2001 nuclear energy was the 2nd highest source of energy. However, it declined through 2019. Today, it is again the 2nd highest used source of energy.  All of the other energy sources remained somewhat consistent over the span from 2001-20023. 

I am curious as to why nuclear energy use declined from 2005-2019, and then rose up in 2023 to where it was in 2001. I also wonder why the use of coal declined by nearly 40%.


In my community, the use of cleaner/more efficient energy sources has led to an effort to better the environment. For example, solar panels are becoming common all around, as all they require is sunlight to create energy. Also, in surrounding counties the use of wind power has become very common with wind turbines. Also, the reduction in coal has resulted in better air quality in my community.

“Shifts in Power": How the US’s energy creation changed from 2001-2023.

"The Rise of Clean Energy"

raw_comment:
1. I notice that coal and natural gas flip flopped in usage over the span of 20 years. Solar appeared soon after 2012 and had some gain above some others. Highest renewable form of energy is wind energy and it is only 10% of all the energy in the U S in 2023. There is much more non renewable energy (Natural Gas, Nuclear, and Coal). It is good though that we are seeing some increase in renewable energy still and at the rate it is going it will keep increasing.

2. Why don’t we try for more renewable? Why isn’t there many laws about renewable energy? Though natural gas may be cheaper why is it used so much even though it is limited?

3. This relates to me and my community because about everyone uses electricity. And not many people know what makes their energy. But some of the easiest energy isn’t the best for the planet. 

4. “The ‘Current’ State of The US”

raw_comment:
What do you notice? 
Coal used to dominate the energy sources, but it went down as natural gas took over its place. Natural gas has had a steady incline through the years, and currently has the majority energy source usage. Nuclear energy usage went down at the exact same time natural gas went up, and spiked around 2020. 
What do you wonder? 
Why did coal have such a steep decline around 2015? Why did nuclear energy go down at the same time natural gas went up? What caused nuclear energy to spike and subsequently decline around 2020?
How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me and my community because I use energy every day. I rely on these energy sources for my daily activities like keeping the lights on, showering, or charging my phone. It also affects the future of our world, which includes my community. Global warming is only getting worse, so the types of energy sources being used in my community (and everywhere else) can have an effect on climate change.

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?

I noticed that in 2020, the percentage of nuclear energy spiked, possibly due to Covid. I also noticed that coal used to be the highest energy source, now it is natural gas. Before 2012, solar energy did not even have a place on the graph but it is now up to 6%. 

2. What do you wonder?

I wonder what caused the spike in nuclear energy in 2020 and if it had anything to do with Covid. I also wonder if the increase in wind energy over the years is because more windmills are being built.

3. How does this relate to you and your community?

I have recently seen more people with solar panels up, which is why solar energy is increasing. I also have been seeing many more electric cars in the area which means we rely less on natural gas to fuel cars. 

4. Create a catchy headline 
“The electric change in electricity sources over the years”
